passage: In a small flat in Toronto, Xin, two and a half, watched Dad rock baby Nadia and hold her rattle. Xin marched over and snatched it. Nadia wailed. Dad didn't call him selfish. "You want Dad too," he said. "Nadia has the rattle now. Xin has the drum. Then it's Xin and Dad and the truck book, just us." Xin banged the drum twice, glanced at Dad, and climbed onto his lap with the book.

qa.q: What did Xin snatch from Nadia?
What might Xin have wanted when he grabbed the rattle?
qa.a: He may have felt left out and wanted to know he still mattered to Dad now that the baby got so much attention.

qa.q: Why did Dad's response work better than calling Xin selfish?
qa.a: It gave Xin his own turn and some one-on-one time without shaming him for what he did. 🙂

qa.q: What was the moment like for Nadia?
qa.a: Nadia was a baby who suddenly lost her rattle, so she was startled and upset, and she needed comfort too.

grounding: Shows an older toddler grabbing a baby's toy out of jealousy and parents giving separate turns and one-on-one time.
